sentences.english: The farmer calls the son.
The son sees a small horse.
The farmer loves the horse.
The son praises the good farmer.
The farmer carries a small gift.
The teacher has a book.
The boy sees the new book.
The teacher teaches the boy.
The boy hears the wise teacher.
The teacher praises the good boy.
The poet seeks the god's sacred temple.

sentences.latin: Poēta deō dōnum novum suum dat.
sentences.english: The poet gives his own new gift to the god.
The sacred temple is guarded by the god.
The wise oracle answers the faithful poet.
And so the poet praises the wise god.

sentences.latin: Rēx fortis urbem magnam et veterem ferōcibus mīlitibus servat.
sentences.english: The brave king protects the great and old city with fierce soldiers.

sentences.latin: Hostis populī ferōx ā duce fidēlī et sapientī dēbellātur.
sentences.english: The people's fierce enemy is conquered by the loyal and wise general.
The king rules the people with just laws.

sentences.latin: Rēx magnus ducem hostium fortem capit.
sentences.english: The great king captures the enemies' brave general.

sentences.latin: Itaque rēx fortis et sapiēns ab omnibus laudātur.
sentences.english: And so the brave and wise king is praised by everyone.
